#Uranium #Silver #Gold #Copper

Inflation is proving sticky. The dollar is near a 19-month high. Metals are feeling the squeeze.

🌎 MACRO
US retail sales rose 0.2% in October, while import prices jumped 1.1% versus 0.7% expected. That keeps pressure on the Fed to tighten. Williams favours further hikes, although he pushed back against more aggressive action.

UK inflation just climbed to 3.6%, but core inflation held at 2.8%. An uncomfortable headline, with less acceleration underneath.

Oil offers some relief: Brent slipped towards $92 after a reported US inventory build. Renewed US–Iran attacks and Hormuz shipping risks could still reverse that move.

☢️ URANIUM
The latest weekly update puts spot at $90.30/lb last Friday, versus a $97 term benchmark at October-end. Utilities are still evaluating offers. My focus remains on signed contracts and the prices needed to bring new supply online.

🥈 SILVER
Around $46 in early trading, down roughly 3%. Higher rate expectations are squeezing precious metals, while silver also carries exposure to industrial demand.

🥇 GOLD
Around $3,778, down nearly 2% and at its lowest since September 2025. A firm dollar and elevated yields are overpowering haven demand.

🔶 COPPER
A stronger dollar and tighter financial conditions remain headwinds. Watch whether physical buying strengthens as prices retreat.

👀 TODAY
Fed minutes at 20:00 CET, US housing data and official oil inventories.

My take: sustained relief in oil, yields and the dollar would give metals breathing room. Until then, strong balance sheets and funding visibility matter.

Long-term bullish. Short-term selective.

The market rewards those who can think in years while everyone else is panicking about the next few weeks.

There’s a lot of talk about agents replacing apps. I think the more interesting future is how they work together.

Word, Excel and PowerPoint are now part of the Copilot experience. And Copilot is becoming part of the apps people have loved and used for decades.

That matters because people have years of muscle memory in these tools. They know how to adjust a spreadsheet, refine a slide, edit a document. That familiarity is an enormous asset to build on.

An agent can do the research, build the model and draft the presentation. You can jump into Excel to check an assumption or PowerPoint to make the story yours, then hand the work back to the agent. Moving between delegation and doing should feel natural.

For agents to become part of everyday work, they need to meet people where they are and work with what they already know.

Apps and agents form an ecosystem. Each makes the other more useful. The agent moves the work forward, and the familiar tools let you shape the result.
